sources.citation: Rathika, G. 2022. An Endangered Tribal Language of Malakkuravan: A Descriptive Study and Documentation. PhD thesis, Department of Linguistics, Annamalai University (guide C. Kuppusamy). Shodhganga hdl.handle.net/10603/641122 (uploaded 22-May-2025).
sources.note: Phonology section gives 27 phonemes (10 vowels + diphthong ai, 16 consonants), allophones, gemination and syllable patterns (V, VC, CV, CVC, CVCC); no suprasegmental section; the words stress/accent/tone/pitch do not occur in the chapter.

sources.citation: Madhava Menon, T. (chief ed.). 1996. The Encyclopaedia of Dravidian Tribes, Vol. II. Thiruvananthapuram: International School of Dravidian Linguistics. Entries 'Mala Kurava - Kerala' (pp. 203-205) and 'Mala Kurava - Tamil Nadu' (pp. 205-206).
sources.note: Nothing. Tamil Nadu entry p. 205 (djvu lines 30649-30652): 'They speak a dialect of Malayalam ("Kuravan Malayalam"), and are bilingual in Tamil, their speech containing many Tamil words and phrases.' Kerala entry quotes Iyer 1937: 'Pandi Kuravans speak Tamil'. Ethnographic only.

sources.citation: Somasekharan Nair, P. 1987. Survey of the tribal speech forms of Kerala: some comments on the questionnaires. International Journal of Dravidian Linguistics 16(1): 144-152 (approx.). Trivandrum: Dravidian Linguistics Association.
sources.note: No phonology content. Methodological review; states verbatim: 'In the first publication [Bhattacharya 1976], words from the speech forms of Kanikkar, Mala Ulladan, Malappulayar, Malakkuravan, Vettuvar, Mala Adiyar and Malappandaram are given in 1573 entries. For 550 entries, the author gives etymologies also with the help of cognates from Malayalam dialects.' Cites MaKur. appan 'father', kayuta 'donkey', ari / kuru 'seed / jackfruit seed' (Bhattacharya pp. 112, 114, 159, 201). Establishes that the only linguistic source for mala1459 is a comparative wordlist without an outline grammar.
